english: Let $C$ be the curve given by $x=t^{3}+3t,\ y=t^{4}+2t^{2}$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $P$ be the point on $C$ at which the tangent to $C$ is parallel to the line $4x-3y+5=0$. Then the value of $\dfrac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}$ at $P$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $C$ वक्र $x=t^{3}+3t,\ y=t^{4}+2t^{2}$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$ द्वारा दिया गया है। माना कि $P$ वक्र $C$ पर वह बिन्दु है जिस पर $C$ की स्पर्श रेखा, रेखा $4x-3y+5=0$ के समान्तर है। तब $P$ पर $\dfrac{d^{3}y}{dx^{3}}$ का मान बराबर है
solution_full: $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=3t^{2}+3=3(t^{2}+1)$, which is positive for all $t$, so $x$ is strictly increasing in $t$ and $y$ is a differentiable function of $x$ along the whole curve.
The line $4x-3y+5=0$ has slope $\dfrac43$. The tangent is parallel to it when $\dfrac{4t}{3}=\dfrac43$, i.e. $t=1$. Then $P=(1+3,\ 1+2)=(4,3)$, and $P$ is unique.

For higher derivatives with respect to $x$, differentiate with respect to $t$ and divide by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ each time: $\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{4t}{3}\right)}{3(t^{2}+1)}=\dfrac{4}{9(t^{2}+1)}$.
(Forgetting the division by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ in the last step gives $-\dfrac{8}{36}=-\dfrac29$, option (B).)
originality_note: New: a parametric pair chosen so that the common factor t^2 + 1 cancels in dy/dx (dy/dx = 4t/3), which turns a third-order parametric derivative into a short exact computation at a point fixed by a tangent-direction condition (way 4, hidden simplification). Closest known: textbook d^2y/dx^2 exercises on standard parametric curves (x = a cos^3 t, cycloid). Different because: the third derivative is asked, the point is fixed through the tangent condition, and the repeated division by dx/dt is the trap.

concept_use.Higher order derivatives: d^2y/dx^2 and then d^3y/dx^3 are computed; the question asks for the third derivative at P.
concept_use.Parametric Differentiation: Every x-derivative is (d/dt of the previous one)/(dx/dt) for x = t^3 + 3t, y = t^4 + 2t^2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function has a stated domain, every symbol is introduced before use, every condition is given, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy/mpmath and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that x is strictly increasing in t (so y = y(x) is well defined), that P is unique (t = 1), that the sign and value -1/27 match only (A), and that a numeric third derivative of y(x) at x = 4 gives -0.0370370. Distractors: missing division by dx/dt (B), sign slip (C), wrong power of t^2 + 1 (D). Changed: No change.
key_step: Seeing dy/dx = 4t/3 and dividing by dx/dt at every further step to reach d^3y/dx^3.
justification: A third-order parametric derivative with two easy-to-miss divisions by dx/dt, plus locating P from the tangent direction; two linked steps rather than one move. Close to the derivative-chain anchor 2025-P2-Q14 (L3), slightly helped by options.
